summary: The unit is sound in its readings of the names and verbs, and it follows Rashi and Ibn Ezra on 'Japheth the elder'. Its faults are in the notes and the rulings: the Rashi summary on 10:25 puts the dispersion at the end of Eber's days where Rashi says Peleg's; the 10:25 note and apparatus credit Radak and Sforno with a reading of נִפְלְגָה (a division of the earth or of lifespans) that neither gives; the grammar of 10:25 says יֻלַּד has no subject, though שְׁנֵי בָנִים is its subject; and Rashi's gloss on עֵבֶר in 10:21 is mistranslated as 'the river was Shem'. The English of the list of Joktan's sons (10:26-28) closes with 'and' and a full stop in each verse although the list runs on to 10:29. Smaller fixes: the sense of אָב, the count in the construct chain of 10:21, the accents of 10:21, and a missing sense for Lud.

patches.value: Children were born to Shem also, the father of all the sons of Eber, the brother of Japheth the elder.
patches.reason: The Hebrew has no 'and' before אֲחִי: 'father of all the sons of Eber' and 'brother of Japheth the elder' are two titles of Shem in apposition, and the added 'and' makes them read as a list. 'Also' is placed next to Shem, whom גַּם־הוּא stresses.

value.english: Children were born to Shem also
value.literal: 'and-to-Shem was-born also he'; the impersonal Pual is rendered as a plural to give the sense that sons were born

value.english: the father of all the sons of Eber
the brother of Japheth the elder
value.literal: 'brother-of Japheth the-elder'; a second title of Shem, with no 'and' in the Hebrew; הגדול is read with Japheth (Rashi, Ibn Ezra)

patches.reason: The new English changed the first and third fragments.
Shem is not the father of the sons of Eber but their forebear, five generations up (10:22-24); the sense is 'ancestor' (4). Sense 2 is the father of a people in the sense of God as father of Israel.

patches.value: construct state; here 'ancestor', not the father in the first generation
patches.reason: Follows the corrected sense.

value: יֻלַּד is a Pual perfect 3ms with no stated subject; Radak says it is general, 'children were born'.
גַּם־הוּא 'he also': the line resumes Shem after the sons of Ham and Japheth have been listed (Ramban).
אֲבִי כָּל־בְּנֵי־עֵבֶר is a construct chain of four nouns, 'father-of all-of sons-of Eber': the first three are in the construct state and only עֵבֶר is absolute.
הַגָּדוֹל after Japheth is ambiguous in the Hebrew: it can describe Japheth or Shem.

The etnaḥta on הוּא divides the verse: the first half says that Shem had children; the second gives two titles of Shem, 'father of all the sons of Eber' and 'brother of Japheth the elder', set apart by the zaqef on עֵבֶר. Silluq closes the verse on הַגָּדוֹל.
patches.reason: The chain אֲבִי כָּל בְּנֵי עֵבֶר has four nouns, not three. The accent note left out the etnaḥta, the main divider of the verse, and called the pashta and zaqef dividers of 'clauses': the second half has no clause, only two phrases in apposition.

patches.value: proper name; on Ibn Ezra's reading the ancestor of the Hebrews (עִבְרִים); Rashi takes עֵבֶר here as the land beyond the River
patches.reason: The learner should know that the word is read two ways here; see the apparatus.

value: עֵבֶר: the man Eber of 10:24-25, whose descendants are the Hebrews (Ibn Ezra), or the land beyond the River, עֵבֶר הַנָּהָר, whose people all descend from Shem (Rashi, Ramban).
הַגָּדוֹל: Japheth the elder (Rashi, Ibn Ezra, most commentators) or Shem the elder brother of Japheth (Ramban, Radak, and some cited by Ibn Ezra).
Onkelos: וּלְשֵׁם אִתְיְלִיד אַף הוּא ... אֲחוּהִי דְיֶפֶת רַבָּא, with the same ambiguity.
patches.reason: The reading of עֵבֶר is ruled 'records' in the commentary but not recorded in the apparatus beside the other alternative of the verse; 'some in Ibn Ezra' is made clear.

patches.value: Rashi: עֵבֶר here is '[beyond] the River' (עֵבֶר הַנָּהָר): Shem was the father of all who lived beyond the River. On this reading 'the sons of Eber' are the people of a region, not the descendants of the man Eber.
patches.reason: הַנָּהָר הָיָה שֵׁם does not say 'the river was Shem'. It completes עֵבֶר as עֵבֶר הַנָּהָר and names Shem as the father of those beyond it (Ramban: אֲבִי כָּל יוֹשְׁבֵי עֵבֶר הַנָּהָר).

patches.value: Ibn Ezra: 'father of all the sons of Eber' makes Shem known as the father of the Hebrews: none stands above him, and the LORD is his God, as in 'the LORD, the God of the Hebrews' (Exod 10:3). Canaan is the father of those below whom there is none, and holy is not to be mixed with profane.
patches.reason: The summary added 'Eber is a person', which the comment does not say, and left out 'and the LORD is his God' with its proof text, the point of the comment.
The entry for לוּד lists a sense, and it fits: Lud the son of Shem, eponym of the people. The translator's rules require it.

patches.value: Radak: the descendants begin with the youngest, Aram, because the list of Shem's sons ended with him. Those of Elam, Asshur and Lud are not given, as there was no need; Aram's are, perhaps because Terah's family married into Aram's line, so that Nahor named his firstborn Uz and a grandson Aram. For Mash, Chronicles has Meshech.
patches.reason: Radak does not say the other sons were 'left without descendants'; he says their descendants are not recorded. The summary also left out his reason for recording Aram's line.

patches.value: pausal form of שֶׁלַח (10:24.5): under the etnaḥta the segol becomes qameṣ
patches.reason: The true pausal change of the verse is here; a learner will otherwise read שָׁלַח and שֶׁלַח as two names.

patches.value: in pause under silluq; the form is the same as in context
patches.reason: עֵ֫בֶר keeps its context vowels in pause; 'pausal form' suggests a changed form.

patches.value: Pual perfect 3ms; its subject is the plural שְׁנֵי בָנִים that follows: a verb placed before its subject may stay singular (Radak: 'in a general way', as in 41:50)
patches.reason: The verb is not impersonal here: שְׁנֵי בָנִים is its subject.

value: יֻלַּד is singular, but its subject is the plural שְׁנֵי בָנִים, which follows it: a verb placed before its subject may keep the singular (Radak: said 'in a general way').
פֶּלֶג and נִפְלְגָה share the root פלג: a wordplay in the explanation of the name.
The accents mark שֵׁם הָאֶחָד פֶּלֶג off from the 'for' clause.
שֵׁם אָחִיו has no verb; the nominal clause runs on from the previous one.
patches.reason: The first note said that the Pual has no subject; in this verse שְׁנֵי בָנִים is its subject, unlike 10:21.

patches.value: the earth stands for its peoples: Rashi, they were scattered and divided over the whole world
patches.reason: The learner needs to see that it is the people of the earth that were divided, as Rashi and the English 'follows' ruling read it.

patches.value: Rashi and Radak take 'the earth was divided' as the dispersion of the peoples. They differ on its time: Rashi, after Seder Olam, puts it at the end of Peleg's days, in the year of his death; Radak says that when Peleg was born the dispersion was already being prepared. Radak ties the shortening of lifespans to the name Joktan, Sforno to the dispersion; neither takes נִפְלְגָה itself to mean it. The English keeps the plain verb.
patches.reason: Radak does not make 'the earth was divided' refer to the shortening of lifespans: he names Peleg for the dispersion and Joktan for the smallness of years (radak:10:25:5).

value: נִפְלְגָה: the division of the earth's peoples at the dispersion (Rashi, Radak, Sforno). Its time: at the end of Peleg's days, in the year of his death (Rashi, after Seder Olam), or already in preparation when he was born (Radak).
patches.reason: No commentator in the pack reads נִפְלְגָה as a division of the land itself or of lifespans; Radak and Sforno both speak of the dispersion. The real difference among them is the time of the dispersion.

patches.value: Rashi: the languages were confused, and the people scattered from the valley and were divided over the whole world. Eber was a prophet, who named his son for what was to come. Seder Olam teaches that the division came at the end of Peleg's days: not at their start, for his younger brother Joktan had already fathered many families, and not in their middle, for Scripture would have said so; so it fell in the year Peleg died.
patches.reason: בְּסוֹף יָמָיו refers to Peleg (בְיָמָיו in the verse), not Eber, as Rashi's conclusion בִּשְׁנַת מוֹת פֶּלֶג shows; the summary said 'the end of Eber's days'.

verdicts.comment: Rashi reads עֵבֶר as the land beyond the River; Ibn Ezra reads 'father of the Hebrews', the line named for Eber, and Ramban cites Ibn Ezra and Radak for Eber as the man. The normative commentators differ, so the English may follow Ibn Ezra; Rashi's reading is recorded in the commentary and, with the patch, in the apparatus.
Explains why Japheth and not Ham is named; the English renders 'brother of Japheth' as written.
Ibn Ezra's own view is that Japheth is the elder.
The plain 'the earth was divided' carries Rashi's dispersion; the summary is corrected on whose days are meant.
A homily on the name Joktan.
Aggadic note on the name Hazarmaveth; the English keeps the name.
